summary: Indictments, convictions, plea deals, sentencing, regulatory enforcement actions, and corporate misconduct cases. The story is the legal action itself, not the political fallout.
fits_when: primary_entities includes a named defendant, prosecutor's office, court, or enforcement body
row.factual_conflicts is empty OR conflicts only on penalties (not on whether charges exist)
fits_poorly_when: story is about political reaction to a case (use geopolitics or policy)
story is about market impact of a settlement (use finance)
case is rumored / unsourced — gates at stage 2 as 'insufficient'

preferred_pattern.describes: what specifically is at stake — a sentence, a fine ceiling, an industry effect
what the filing alleges (the count or charge)
the supporting fact (a number, a date, an action)
verbatim from the filing or an official statement
next procedural date — sentencing, hearing, response deadline

notes: Quote module is preferred when a filing or DOJ statement is in 02_evidence.quotes — case copy is always stronger than paraphrase.
Map module is rarely useful for legal-scandal; only include if the case has a clear geographic anchor (cross-border fraud, multi-district indictment).

asset_hint_policy.data: use for any module asserting a count, dollar figure, or sentencing range; reference the numeric_fact_id
asset_hint_policy.mute: default; use when the spoken claim is the asset
asset_hint_policy.map: only when the case spans named jurisdictions (e.g., multi-district indictment); requires labels
asset_hint_policy.photo: PROHIBITED for legal-scandal modules — see banned_visual_patterns

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Mugshot or perp-walk imagery of a defendant
banned_visual_patterns.why: Implies guilt before adjudication and is editorial posturing
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Use data module with the count list, or mute

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Dramatic courthouse exterior with red color overlay
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Use a labelled jurisdiction map only if multi-district; otherwise mute

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Stock photo of a person in handcuffs
banned_visual_patterns.why: Generic stock implies a specific identity; visual-safety/identity-implication blocker

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Logo of the defendant company filling the frame
banned_visual_patterns.why: Reads as brand attack rather than reporting on the case
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Logo permitted as L3 attribution only; not as primary asset

lead_with: the charging document or filed complaint
the official statement from the prosecutor's office
second_tier: Reuters / AP / FT wire reporting that quotes the filing
the defendant's own statement or response
treat_with_caution: social media posts unless from the official body's account
must_cite_explicitly: every count number ('17 counts of wire fraud')
every sentencing or settlement dollar figure

patterns.name: indictment
patterns.example: The SDNY charged Sam Bankman-Fried with seven counts of wire fraud and conspiracy on Tuesday.

patterns.name: verdict
patterns.shape: <defendant> was convicted on <n> of <m> counts in <court> on <date>.
patterns.example: Elizabeth Holmes was convicted on 4 of 11 counts in San Jose federal court.

patterns.name: settlement
patterns.example: Meta agreed to pay $1.4 billion to settle Texas's facial-recognition lawsuit.

patterns.name: sentencing
patterns.example: Elizabeth Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison.

first_4_words_must_contain: the body bringing the action (DOJ, SEC, SDNY, FTC, EU Commission)
banned_constructions: speculative outcome ('faces life in prison' before sentencing)

good: The SDNY charged Sam Bankman-Fried with seven counts of wire fraud on Tuesday.
FTX founder pleaded guilty to two counts in federal court Wednesday.
The SEC fined Goldman Sachs $400 million for record-keeping failures.
bad: A shocking scandal has emerged at the heart of the financial industry.
Could SBF face life in prison?
The disgraced founder may finally face justice.

subtitle_guidance.L1_role: the count, charge, or settlement number
L2_rules: name the court or body explicitly
L3_rules: L3 is mandatory for every evidence and quote module in legal-scandal
if the only source is wire reporting, attribute the wire ('Reuters · DOJ filing')
type_specific_rules: Defendant's name appears as L1 only when the news IS the conviction/sentencing of that named individual; otherwise the body bringing the action takes L1.
Never use a defendant's photo with their name as L1 — use a data module.
If charges are alleged (not yet adjudicated), L1 must say 'CHARGED' or 'INDICTED', never 'GUILTY'.

module_selection_hints.include_quote_when: 02_evidence.quotes contains a verbatim line from the filing, the prosecutor's statement, or the defendant's response
module_selection_hints.include_map_when: the case is multi-district / cross-border AND the geographic split is load-bearing to the story
module_selection_hints.include_data_when: the story has a count list, a settlement figure, a sentencing range, OR a comparison to prior cases
module_selection_hints.min_attribution_per_module: every evidence and quote module must have L3 source attribution; L3 may not be empty
module_selection_hints.stakes_module_must_name: either the maximum penalty (with attribution to statute) OR the affected counterparty (shareholders, customers, regulators)

anti_patterns.pattern: Treating an indictment as a conviction
anti_patterns.shape: Hook says 'guilty' when only charges have been filed
anti_patterns.fix: Use 'charged' / 'indicted'; reserve 'guilty' for plea or verdict

anti_patterns.shape: Stakes leans on adjectives instead of facts
anti_patterns.fix: Stakes states the count, the maximum penalty, or the affected counterparty

anti_patterns.pattern: Quoting a paraphrase from a wire as if it were the filing
anti_patterns.shape: Quote module text is from a Reuters summary, not the filing itself
anti_patterns.fix: Pull the quote text from 02_evidence.quotes only when the filing or official statement is the source

anti_patterns.why: Speculation rendered as forward look; banned hedge
anti_patterns.fix: Close anchors on the next procedural date: sentencing hearing, response deadline, appeal window

anti_patterns.pattern: Using a defendant's logo or photo as primary asset
anti_patterns.shape: Module fills frame with company logo or person's headshot
anti_patterns.fix: Logos and identity imagery permitted only as L3-size attribution chips; primary asset is data or mute

anti_patterns.pattern: Treating regulators and prosecutors as interchangeable
anti_patterns.shape: Script says 'the SEC charged' when it was actually the DOJ
anti_patterns.why: Civil vs criminal distinction is load-bearing for legal-scandal
anti_patterns.fix: Match the body to the action: DOJ/USAO for criminal charges; SEC/CFTC/FTC for civil; mention both when both acted

stage_2_extra_checks: verify the charging document is in 02_evidence.source_documents (case docket entry, complaint, or official press release)
every count number must have source_ids pointing to the filing or the press release that lists it
if the only source for a count is wire reporting, treat as single-source (script must say 'according to <wire>')
stage_5_extra_checks: scan 03_script.md for the words 'guilty', 'convicted', 'pleaded guilty' — verify each is consistent with the case stage in 01_understanding
verify no module has asset_hint:'photo' (legal-scandal prohibits)
verify every L1 in subtitle layer corresponds to a count, charge, or settlement number — not the defendant's name unless the news is their conviction
